About

Engineering meets intelligence

I am an aeronautical engineer and AI researcher with a background spanning the full lifecycle of aviation — from the physics of flight and propulsion systems to the data-driven methods that will define the next generation of aerospace engineering.

Originally from Syria, I arrived in the UK with one goal: to become a researcher who contributes meaningfully to engineering and aviation. I built toward that deliberately — studying at the University of Salford, gaining real flight experience, working within British Airways operational environments, pursuing AI at the University of Leeds, and applying to Cranfield University's CDT in Net Zero Aviation.

My work sits at the intersection of sustainable aviation, propulsion system design, novel aircraft configurations, and AI-driven engineering optimisation. I believe the next breakthroughs in aviation will come from people who can hold both the physics and the computation simultaneously.

Research

Current & forthcoming

Research at the frontier of sustainable aviation — connecting novel configurations, propulsion engineering, and AI-driven design.

Active Research Interest
Assessment of Novel Aircraft Configurations Impact on Engine Design
The aviation industry is pursuing radical new airframe configurations — blended wing bodies, truss-braced wings, distributed propulsion — that offer step-change efficiency improvements but fundamentally change the design requirements for the propulsion system. On a blended wing body, engines mount on the upper rear body rather than under the wing, changing intake geometry, distortion characteristics, and structural load paths entirely. This research systematically assesses how novel configurations change engine requirements, combining multidisciplinary design analysis with AI-accelerated design space exploration.
InstitutionCranfield University
SupervisorDr Christos Mourouzidis

01

SECR Sustainability Carbon Reporting — Data Mining Research

AI-driven SECR carbon footprint analysis. Novel synthetic data generation methodology for sustainability reporting models. 89% accuracy on real datasets. University of Leeds, 2025–2026.

02

Net Zero Aviation Technology Pathways — Systems Analysis

Full lifecycle analysis of net zero aviation technologies — electrification, hydrogen, SAF, and hybrid systems — with focus on systems-level interdependencies between fuel production, aircraft design, infrastructure, and emissions.

03

AI for Aerospace Design Space Exploration

Applying machine learning surrogate models to accelerate multidisciplinary design optimisation of aerospace systems. Focus on how propulsion performance varies across novel airframe configurations faster than traditional CFD approaches allow.
